page: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel CPU cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache.

The Intel processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512f, AVX512_vnni, AVX_vnni, AVX512_bf16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_tile, AMX_int8), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates average performance across most CPU-bound tasks. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1877.0 and a multi-core score of 7215.0, with a PassMark CPU score of 12045.57. Software compilation via Clang registers at 8701.0, while static web serving throughput reaches 11.89 GB/sec.

Despite solid compute capabilities, memory performance represents a notable tradeoff. The PassMark memory score of 1718.22 is categorized in the bottom 25%, and large-block memory write bandwidth is limited to 40.33 GB/sec. Additionally, while prompt processing for a 7B LLM model reaches 52.37 tokens/sec, text generation for the same model drops to a weak 7.92 tokens/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for compute-heavy workloads with low memory footprints, such as software compilation, lightweight web serving, and basic vector-accelerated processing, rather than memory-intensive databases or large language model text generation.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel cores and 16 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX to drive compute workloads. Benchmark results place its CPU performance in the average tier, with a PassMark CPU score of 12045.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7215.0. However, memory performance is a clear tradeoff, with a PassMark memory score in the bottom 25% and weak text generation speeds on 7B LLM models. This resource profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for CPU-focused tasks like software compilation, image processing, and static web serving, while rendering it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or complex language model inference.
